Name: Request
Keywords: request; response; api call; http call; round trip; rpc; generic traffic
Use When: THE DEFAULT -- the plain dot; pick it whenever no other payload row names the cargo; generic request/response hops and any edge whose traffic has no identity worth drawing
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never swap the dot for a themed glyph as decoration when the cargo really is a plain call

Name: Chat Message
Keywords: chat message; im; direct message; chat bubble; sent message; conversation; group chat
Use When: chat and IM payloads; websocket fanout of user messages; group-chat delivery hops; the message body moving between chat servers
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never reuse the bubble for system notifications -- fire-and-forget cargo is event

Name: Email
Keywords: email; mail; smtp; inbox; mail delivery; transactional email; newsletter
Use When: mail payloads; transactional email hops; the SMTP relay legs of a notification story; queued mail draining to a provider
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never use the envelope as a generic message stand-in -- chat cargo is message

Name: File
Keywords: file; blob; upload; download; attachment; document transfer; object
Use When: file and blob transfer; uploads landing in object storage; document sync legs; CDN asset fetches
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never use for raw bytes that never form a whole file -- that is binary-stream

Name: Binary Stream
Keywords: binary; bytes; byte stream; raw stream; tensor; video bytes; replication wire; on the wire
Use When: raw byte or tensor streams; the replication wire between database nodes; video byte transport; any cargo whose content is machine-readable bits rather than a named document
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; the 101 text is decorative (aria-hidden) so the label carries the meaning; never use for a finished file -- that is file

Name: Token
Keywords: token; jwt; session token; credential; access token; bearer; api key
Use When: credential and session-token hops; JWT handoffs in an auth flow; API keys presented to a gateway; refresh legs
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never print a real secret value in the label -- name the credential type not its contents

Name: Query
Keywords: query; sql; database query; search request; lookup; read request; index scan
Use When: database queries and search requests; the read leg travelling INTO a datastore or search index
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never use for the result coming back -- the return leg carries whatever the query produced (rows; file; media)

Name: Event
Keywords: event; domain event; notification; pubsub event; emitted event; webhook; published event
Use When: domain events; pub/sub publishes; notifications and webhooks; anything fire-and-forget travelling to subscribers
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never use the ping for a call that awaits a reply -- an event has no response leg to draw

Name: Transaction
Keywords: transaction; payment; charge; settlement; ledger entry; invoice; payout
Use When: payments and financial transfers; ledger writes; the settlement legs of a checkout story
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never use for a plain database write with no money in it -- that is query or request

Name: Media
Keywords: media; audio; video; stream chunk; playback; frame; hls segment
Use When: audio and video media payloads; playback and streaming segments; transcode hops between media services
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo; never use for the raw bytes of a non-media transfer -- that is binary-stream

Name: Feedback
Keywords: feedback; review comment; critique; verdict; change request; revision; sign off; human label; moderation decision
Use When: a judgement ABOUT a work item travelling back to whoever can act on it: review comments returning to the author, a moderation or canary verdict returning to the pipeline that asked for it, a human label going back into a training set, and -- in the process genre -- the cargo of the loop-closing edge, where it carries what the next cycle will do differently
Don't: never icon-only -- the edge label still names the cargo and WHO gave it; never use it for a plain success/error response to a call the sender is waiting on -- that is request coming back; never for a fire-and-forget notification with nobody expected to act -- that is event
